source: Preserved legacy baseline contract for current-code legacy dashboard path tests

interpretation.what_this_contract_is: A REPRODUCIBILITY contract, not a correctness one. It asserts that current code reproduces the preserved legacy behaviour exactly. As of 2026-08-27 that behaviour is known to include a capture defect, so a passing run asserts we reproduce the defect faithfully. Do not cite a green result as evidence that the captured tensor is correct.
interpretation.activation_rows_max_abs_delta: KEEP at 0. Still correct: no scenario here sets `capture_hook_name`, so the legacy path resolves the declared hook as before. Exact equality remains the right assertion because nothing about this path changed.
interpretation.imported_activation_rows: KEEP as regression anchors; QUARANTINE the reading. These counts were produced at `blocks.{N}.hook_mlp_in`, which is not the tensor these transcoders were trained on. Valid for detecting drift in the legacy path, invalid as any statement about correct data.
interpretation.generation_throughput_relative_tolerance: KEEP as a performance-regression guard. STRUCTURALLY BLIND to capture location: wall time is dominated by forward passes, which the hook does not change. Measured 2026-08-27, two layers whose stored output differed by 27% finished within 7 ms of each other. `throughput was within tolerance` is therefore never evidence about which tensor was captured.
interpretation.import_wall_relative_tolerance: KEEP for the legacy path. INSUFFICIENT for a corrected-hook corpus: import wall tracks row count, and a corrected layer 0 carries about 37% more rows. A corrected path needs its own baseline rather than this tolerance stretched over it.
interpretation.preserved_baseline_lineage: DEFECT-BEARING ON PURPOSE. `saelens 3eea6552` predates the capture fix. Do not advance these pins to make a failing test pass: the pins are what make the baseline reproducible, and moving them silently redefines what is being compared.
interpretation.trip_hazard_capture_hook_name: `resolve_capture_hook_name` is called in NeuronpediaRunner.__init__, ABOVE the legacy/columnar split, so it governs the legacy path too. This contract is safe today only because no scenario sets `capture_hook_name`, i.e. by absence rather than by design. If one ever does, every stored value here invalidates at once, and the failure will present as a row-count regression rather than as a changed capture location. Look here first.
interpretation.acceptance_check_lives_elsewhere: Implied L0 is the absolute check for capture location, and it deliberately does NOT belong in this file: the preserved baseline is defective by design and would fail its own gate on every run. It belongs at the generation acceptance gate. See interpretune docs/verifying_dashboard_generation.md.
